conductSummary: Using force, threat, or deception to remove or restrain a person for a purpose listed in division (A), or knowingly doing so under the harm conditions in division (B). For a victim under thirteen or mentally incompetent, the statute covers removal or restraint by any means. The listed purposes include ransom, facilitating a felony, terrorizing or serious harm, nonconsensual sexual activity, compelling governmental action, and involuntary servitude.
gradeSummary: F1 ordinarily. Safe unharmed release reduces violations of (A)(1)-(5), (B)(1), or (B)(2) to F2, subject to the specification exceptions; it does not reduce (A)(6). Under (C)(3), a victim under thirteen plus a sexual-motivation specification carries fifteen years to life, or ten years to life upon safe unharmed release, instead of the ordinary F1 range. A trafficking specification under 2941.1422 triggers the separate mandatory-prison and restitution rules in 2929.14(B)(7) and 2929.18(B)(8), subject to (C)(3).

conductSummary: Without privilege, knowingly removing someone by force or threat; restraining someone by force or threat under circumstances creating a risk of physical harm or placing the person in fear; or holding someone in involuntary servitude. Division (B) adds sexual motivation, defined by section 2971.01.
gradeSummary: F3 for (A)(1) or (A)(2), including the corresponding sexual-motivation branch in (B). F2 for involuntary servitude under (A)(3), including the corresponding (B) branch. A trafficking specification under 2941.1422 triggers the mandatory-prison and restitution rules in 2929.14(B)(7) and 2929.18(B)(8).

conductSummary: With purpose to obtain a valuable thing or benefit or induce an unlawful act, making a listed threat, committing aggravated menacing or menacing, or using the listed reputational threats. This entry covers division (B), not the separately defined sexual-extortion offense in (D).
gradeSummary: F3 under division (C). Where both extortion and sexual extortion convictions concern the same conduct and victim, division (F) identifies allied offenses of similar import under 2941.25; do not simply add both punishments.

conductSummary: Threatening to release, exhibit, or distribute another person's private images with a listed purpose: compelling an act or omission, inducing an offense, obtaining more private images, or obtaining something of value. The statutory private-images definition and threats by innuendo apply.
gradeSummary: Under (E)(1), F3 ordinarily. Under (E)(2), F2 for a prior (D) conviction or plea, or a victim under eighteen, elderly, or a disabled adult, unless (E)(3) applies. Under (E)(3), F1 for two or more prior (D) convictions or pleas, or the separately stated combination of a prior protected-victim sexual-extortion offense and knowledge or reason to know of the victim's protected status. Same-conduct, same-victim extortion and sexual-extortion convictions are subject to the allied-offense rule in (F).

statutoryName: Extortionate extension of credit - criminal usury
conductSummary: Division (A)(1) only: knowingly making or participating in an extortionate extension of credit, as defined in 2905.21. The definition covers the parties' understanding when credit is extended, or the debtor's later learning, that nonpayment will result in the defined violent or other criminal means of causing harm.
gradeSummary: F4 under division (B). This does not include the separate M1 transaction-record possession branch.

statutoryName: Extortionate extension of credit - criminal usury
conductSummary: Division (A)(2) only: knowingly engaging in criminal usury, as defined in 2905.21. The definition includes credit above twenty-five per cent annual interest, subject to its exceptions for rates otherwise authorized by law and credit between immediate family members.
gradeSummary: F4 under division (B). This does not include the separate M1 transaction-record possession branch.

statutoryName: Extortionate extension of credit - criminal usury
conductSummary: Division (A)(3) only: possessing a writing, paper, instrument, or article used to record criminally usurious transactions, knowing its contents record such a transaction. The definition of criminal usury in 2905.21 applies.
gradeSummary: M1 under division (B). The F4 punishment for (A)(1) and (A)(2) does not apply to this records-possession branch.

conductSummary: Knowingly recruiting, luring, enticing, isolating, harboring, transporting, providing, obtaining, maintaining, or attempting those acts as described in (A). The statute distinguishes knowing exposure to involuntary servitude or compelled sexual activity/performance/material from its minor and developmental-disability branches. Division (B) defines compulsion for (A)(1). Sexual activity or solicitation alone, without more, does not establish this offense under (C).
gradeSummary: F1 with a special custody rule in (E): for conduct on or after March 22, 2019, an indefinite prison sentence with a selected minimum of ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, or fifteen years and maximum determined under 2929.144. For earlier conduct, a definite term selected from those same ten-to-fifteen-year terms. The ordinary three-to-eleven-year F1 minimum does not apply. Conventional fine up to $20,000 under 2929.18(A)(3)(a). Division (D) preserves applicable allied-offense rules for same-conduct, same-victim Chapter 2907 convictions.

statutoryName: Unlawful conduct with respect to documents
conductSummary: Without privilege, knowingly destroying, concealing, removing, confiscating, or possessing another person's actual or purported government identification document or passport in the course of, with intent to violate, or with intent to facilitate one of the nine offenses expressly listed in (A): 2905.01, 2905.02, 2905.32, 2907.21, 2907.22, 2907.32, 2907.321, 2907.322, or 2907.323.
gradeSummary: F3 under division (B). The predicate references define this document offense; this entry does not independently select or approve those other charges.

conductSummary: Knowingly using fire or explosion to create a substantial risk of serious physical harm to another person; cause physical harm to an occupied structure; or, through an agreement for hire or other consideration, create a substantial risk of physical harm to an occupied structure. The statutory occupied-structure definition applies.
gradeSummary: F1 for (A)(1) or (A)(3); F2 for (A)(2), under (B)(2)-(3). Arson-offender registration requirements in 2909.13-2909.15 require separate attention in addition to custody and fines.

conductSummary: Knowingly using fire or explosion to cause or create a substantial risk of physical harm to property under the circumstances in (A) or to a structure that is not an occupied structure under (B). The branches distinguish consent, purpose to defraud, public property, land, and agreements for hire. Division (C) preserves the specified consent affirmative defenses for (B).
gradeSummary: Under (D)(2), (A)(1) and (B)(1) are M1 unless property value or physical harm is $1,000 or more, when they are F4. Under (D)(3), (A)(2), (3), (5), (6), and (B)(3) are F4. Under (D)(4), (A)(4) and (B)(2) are F3. Arson-offender registration requirements in 2909.13-2909.15 require separate attention.

evidence.quote: (3) A violation of division (A)(2), (3), (5), or (6) or (B) (3) of this section is a felony of the fourth degree.
(4) A violation of division (A)(4) or (B) (2) of this section is a felony of the third degree.

conductSummary: Division (A)(1)-(2): purposely by any means, or knowingly by damaging or tampering with property, interrupting or impairing the listed communications, navigation, public transportation, or public utility services. Division (B): knowingly using the listed computer/electronic systems or internet to disrupt, interrupt, or impair police, fire, educational, commercial, or governmental operations. This entry excludes (A)(3), the separate emergency-response branch.
gradeSummary: F4 under division (C), solely for the included (A)(1), (A)(2), and (B) conduct. The unresolved (A)(3) emergency-response dependency is not cleared.

conductSummary: Knowingly causing the harm specified in (A)-(D) to an occupied structure or its contents; another's business property; government property; a cemetery or memorial property; or a place of burial through breaking and entering. The business-property branches distinguish $1,000 value/harm from property necessary to the occupation regardless of value. Division (F) supplies the section's serious-physical-harm and cemetery definitions.
gradeSummary: Under (E), F5 ordinarily with an expressly additional fine up to $2,500 beyond the penalties specified in 2929.11-2929.18. F4 when property value or physical harm is at least $7,500 but below $150,000; F3 at $150,000 or more. The additional F5 fine is separate from the conventional sentencing fine.

conductSummary: This entry covers only (A)(1)-(6): the specified improper tampering/property conduct, offensive-substance devices, survey markers, safety devices, outdoor fires, and computer interference. Each branch retains its stated mental-state and privilege requirements. The own-residential-property branch requires the mortgage and pending-foreclosure conditions. The computer branch requires intent to impair functioning. Critical-infrastructure conduct under (A)(7) is excluded.
gradeSummary: Under (C)(2), (A)(1)-(5) are M3 ordinarily, M1 if they create a risk of physical harm; specified aircraft-property cases are F5 for risk and F4 for substantial risk or occupied aircraft. Under (C)(3), (A)(6) is M1 ordinarily, F5 for value/loss of at least $1,000 but below $10,000, or specified aircraft-computer risk; F4 for value/loss of $10,000 or more, or specified aircraft-computer substantial risk or occupied aircraft. The (A)(7)/(C)(4) F3 branch is not included.

evidence.quote: (2) Except as otherwise provided in this division, criminal mischief committed in violation of division (A)(1), (2), (3), (4), or (5) of this section is a misdemeanor of the third degree.

Except as otherwise provided in this division, if the violation of division (A)(1), (2), (3), (4), or (5) of this section creates a risk of physical harm to any person, criminal mischief committed in violation of division (A)(1), (2), (3), (4), or (5) of this section is a misdemeanor of the first degree.
(3) Except as otherwise provided in this division, criminal mischief committed in violation of division (A)(6) of this section is a misdemeanor of the first degree.
